root_cause: The radios component only updates conditional visibility on click events via handleClick, which loops through all radios with aria-controls. Keyboard navigation fires change events, but the previous handleChange only processed the target input. When arrowing from a radio with aria-controls (text message) to one without (opt-out), the change event fires on the opt-out radio, so the text message's conditional field remains visible.
repair_strategy: Add a change event listener in init() and a handleChange method that loops through all radios with aria-controls (mirroring handleClick), ensuring keyboard selection updates all conditional fields based on current checked states.
expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation (arrow keys) will correctly show/hide conditional fields when moving between radio options, including hiding the mobile number field when opting out after selecting Text message, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Duplicate handling if both click and change events fire for the same interaction, but setAttributes is idempotent.
If another script also listens for change events on the same radios, there could be unintended side effects, though the change event is standard and unlikely to conflict.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the email radio to the text radio hides the email input and shows the mobile number input.
Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the text radio to the opt-out radio hides the mobile number input.
Verify that mouse clicks still correctly show/hide the associated conditional fields.
Verify that the aria-expanded attribute on each radio reflects its checked state after keyboard selection.
